item.title: Youth, 16, arrested for shooting of 19-year-old man in garden
item.description:
Youth, 16, arrested for shooting of 19-year-old man in garden

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A 16-year-old youth has been arrested after a 19-year-old man was shot dead while gardening in Schiedam.

The victim was attacked by three people as he tended the front garden of a house in Weverpad with two other people on Saturday afternoon. Both his companions were wounded in the incident, but their injuries are not life-threatening.

One was taken to hospital for treatment, while the other suffered minor injuries and fled the scene. He was arrested by police but has since been released and is not regarded as a suspect.

Police arrested the 16-year-old male youth in Capelle aan den IJssel on Tuesday afternoon on suspicion of murder or attempted murder. The search for the other two suspected assailants is ongoing.

The shooting may have been a case of mistaken identity, police said. A large-scale inquiry led by the prosecution service is ongoing.

The town’s mayor, Harold Bergmann, has placed security cameras outside the scene of the shooting and two nearby houses where explosions took place the following day. Police have not established if the incidents are linked.

item.title: NL and Germany sign deal on faster, more frequent trains
item.description:
NL and Germany sign deal on faster, more frequent trains

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands and Germany have agreed to increase the number of trains running between them and cut travel times, with a focus on shortening the route to Berlin.

Annet Bertram, junior minister for public transport and rail, signed a joint declaration with German transport minister Steffen Bilger in Berlin on Tuesday. The agreement covers cross-border passenger and freight traffic, including military transport.

Bertram, of the centrist Christian Democrat CDA, told broadcaster NOS that she had wanted to travel to Berlin by train, but that current diversions made it impossible. “That is exactly why it is important that we discuss these issues in Berlin now,” she said.

The two countries will improve the main border routes and give new rail operators more access to the network.

The journey from Amsterdam to Berlin, 660km, takes almost seven hours, compared with three and a half hours for the 500km trip to Paris, according to NOS.

National rail operator NS and Deutsche Bahn run just four direct trains to Berlin, and all of them will be cancelled for three months next spring because of engineering work.

“Interest is not the problem, speed is,” Bertram said. She told NOS she would like to see “several options an hour” to Berlin or Frankfurt within 10 to 15 years.

item.title: Court upholds licence for Amsterdam TikTok sensation Fabel Friet
item.description:
Court upholds licence for Amsterdam TikTok sensation Fabel Friet

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amsterdam city council was entitled to extend the licence for a chip shop whose long queues have been blamed by local residents for damaging the quality of life in the city centre neighbourhood, a court has ruled.

A judge said campaigners had failed to show that the problems were solely or mainly caused by customers of Fabel Friet, which has become a magnet for tourists drawn by the social media platform TikTok.

The decision is a setback for locals who wanted the court to overturn an extension to Fabel Friet’s licence, which was granted by the city council in 2024. The court was not asked to rule on the current licence issued this year.

They said the queues at the outlet in Runstraat, stretching back to the canal bridge, added to problems with overcrowding in the Negen Straatjes district  and attracted seagulls to the area.

“The number of places where they can sit and eat their chips without causing a nuisance is quite limited,” resident Niek van der Heijden told the court at an earlier hearing.

But judges said Fabel Friet was not primarily responsible for the queues and litter problems and the licence was granted correctly.

Exotic toppings

“Other catering outlets in the neighbourhood also attract large numbers of visitors and have queues,” the court said in a press release.

“The court concludes that it cannot be assumed that the problems experiences are solely or primarliy caused by customers of Fabel Friet. The neighbouring residents have not demonstrated this.”

Fabel Friet’s founders, Abel Klatzer and Floris Feilzer, have opened four other branches in the city centre since they launched the business in 2020, but the outlet in Runstraat remains their flagship.

Tourists flocked to the shop after their videos of their fries topped with exotic toppings such as Parmesan cheese and truffle mayonnaise were widely shared on TikTok.

The owners set up a special queueing system and hired extra security to try to keep order in the neighbourhood. At one stage they also employed a falconer to keep away the seagulls that ripped open the rubbish bags outside the shop and spilled the contents all over the street.

item.title: Johan Cruyff’s grandson called up to play for USA under-18 team
item.description:
Johan Cruyff’s grandson called up to play for USA under-18 team

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is currently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

His son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

item.title: What’s on at IDFA 2026: five documentaries to watch
item.description:
What’s on at IDFA 2026: five documentaries to watch

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA) opens on Thursday for its 39th edition, with 253 films from 80 countries screening until November 22.

The festival was founded in 1988 by Ally Derks, at a time when documentaries rarely made it into Dutch cinemas. The first edition showed 72 films to around 2,000 visitors.

There are prizes for the best films in the International Competition and the Envision Competition, which is for more experimental work.

There are also prizes for the best debut, the best Dutch film and the best use of archive footage. The winners will be announced on November 19.

Here are some highlights to look out for:

White Tiger Column
The opening film follows a group of young recruits through 45 days of training at a jungle camp run by Myanmar’s resistance movement. Canadian directors Robert Mentov, Dwight Jantzi and Bryan Dickie filmed the volunteers’ daily routines as they prepare to fight. The film is in the International Competition and is also nominated for the award for best first feature.

You Can See Everything
Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of blood-testing company Theranos, invited comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim into her home in the weeks before she went to prison. They filmed her daily life with her partner, hotel heir Billy Evans, and their two children. The film was made in secret from 2023 and unveiled at a surprise screening at the Telluride film festival in September.

Musk
Oscar winner Alex Gibney’s portrait of Elon Musk runs to almost four hours. Gibney expanded the film after Musk briefly became one of President Trump’s closest aides and set about cutting the federal government. The film premiered at the Venice film festival in September.

30 mei, 1969 (gritu di un pueblo)
On May 30, 1969, aworkers in Curaçao went on strike, which grew into a popular uprising against exploitation and inequality. The Dutch government sent troops to the island, causing political turmoil. Curaçao-born filmmaker John Leerdam made the film 25 years later, interviewing people who were involved and drawing on archive footage. It first screened at IDFA in 1995, and is returning this year in a new restoration by Amsterdam’s Eye Filmmuseum.

No Man’s Air
On July 20, 1974, the last flight landed at Nicosia Airport before Turkey invaded Cyprus. The airport has sat ever since in the no man’s land between the Greek and Turkish parts of the island. In this 42-minute film, Dutch filmmakers Peter Delpeut and Gerco de Ruijter use found footage to reconstruct that flight, with the Cypriot captain narrating off screen.

item.title: No sign of breakthrough as deadline looms on Dutch tax plans
item.description:
No sign of breakthrough as deadline looms on Dutch tax plans

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch government is running out of time to find a majority in parliament for its tax programme for next year, with no sign of a breakthrough in negotiations with opposition parties.

Prime minister Rob Jetten has repeatedly said he wants to secure a broad agreement with concessions on the left and right, but the two sides’ demands are proving irreconcilable.

Junior finance minister Eelco Eerenberg, who is responsible for the tax plans, called on MPs to “look with a clear head and a new day at what is on the table”, at the end of a debate that brought the parties no closer to ending the deadlock.

The minority coalition of D66, CDA and VVD need to find 10 votes in the lower house and 17 votes in the Senate from at least two opposition parties to pass their legislation.

The parties have until 2pm on Wednesday to table fresh amendments, after which the tax plans will go to a vote in the lower house, which is scheduled for Thursday. The Senate is due to vote in December.

The left-wing Pro, who have teamed up the pro-European liberal minor party Volt, are pressing the cabinet to raise another €1.5 billion in taxes on people with high levels of assets and savings to fund tax cuts for working people.

But the move is being blocked by the right-wing liberal VVD, who favour doing a deal instead with a right-wing block of JA21, the farmers’ party BBB and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

Split vote

The coalition parties have not ruled out splitting their vote on Pro’s amendement, an unprecedented move that would allow D66, CDA and Pro to pass the measure with support from other opposition groups while the VVD vote against.

The tax service has warned that if the plans are not passed before November 20 it will not be able to include the new rates in next year’s tax demands, meaning millions of taxpayers will be sent incorrect bills that have to be adjusted later.

Employers’ payslips will also be calculated on the basis of the 2026 rates for at least the first quarter.

With the prospect of a cabinet collapse looming, MPs backed a motion on Tuesday requiring parliament to explore alternative combinations before resorting to fresh elections.

The motion, tabled by the Christian parties ChristenUnie, SGP and CDA, would change the parliament’s procedural rules, to say MPs “will consult on a new formation” after a cabinet resigns rather than “can consult”.

Only one of the last seven Dutch governments has lasted the full term and a general election in March 2027, the earliest it could be held, would be the third in less than three and a half years.

item.title: Unemployment rising faster for people with foreign roots
item.description:
Unemployment rising faster for people with foreign roots

November 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Unemployment is rising faster among people with foreign roots in the Netherlands, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS.

Joblessness among first-generation immigrants rose from 5.8% in 2024 to 6.9% in the first three quarters of this year. Among the second generation, people born in the Netherlands with at least one parent born abroad, it went from 5.3% to 6%.

Among people born in the Netherlands to two Dutch-born parents, the rise was minimal: from 2.9% to 3%. Overall unemployment went up from 3.7% to 4%.

Part of the reason for the gap is that immigrants are generally younger, and young people are more likely to be out of work, the CBS said.

Among 15- to 25-year-olds, 15.3% of first-generation immigrants in the labour force were jobless this year, up from 12.9% in 2024. Among young people of Dutch origin the rate was 7%, roughly the same as two years ago.

The gap is also widening in older age groups. Unemployment among immigrants aged 25 to 45 rose from 5.9% to 6.6%, compared with 2.2% for people of Dutch origin.

The difference between immigrants and the national average had been shrinking until 2022 and then held steady until 2024, before starting to widen again last year.

item.title: Senators back plan to cultivate embryos for scientific research
item.description:
Senators back plan to cultivate embryos for scientific research

November 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch senate has approved plans to allow specially grown embryos to be used for research into hereditary illnesses and infertility.

The bill, proposed by the liberal parties VVD and D66 during the last cabinet term while D66 was in opposition, achieved a narrow majority of 38 to 35 votes in the upper house.

The Christian parties ChristenUnie and SGP are opposed to cultivating embryos for scientific research because they see it as a violation of the sanctity of life.

The far-right PVV also voted against the plan, which party senator Ilse Bezaan called a “morally reprehensible” measure. “There are good alternatives, we shouldn’t open the door to a sliding scale,” she said.

Until now only embryos that are discarded during IVF treatment could be used for research purposes, but scientists say that using newly fertilised embryos would allow them to study the effect of treatments in the early stages of development.

item.title: Meat sector and government put profits before welfare: report
item.description:
Meat sector and government put profits before welfare: report

November 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch meat industry and the government are both failing to protect animal welfare, and put profits first as the laws are vague and hard to enforce.

“The system is failing to protect animal welfare: the government and the sector are falling short,” the committee, chaired by former transport inspectorate chief Jan van den Bos, said in its final report.

The agriculture ministry set up the panel in 2024 to review oversight of the meat chain. It found that food safety and animal health are well protected.

Welfare is harmed on a large scale even when companies follow the law, the committee said, because legal standards are vague and current production methods and costs are always the starting point when they are set.

Some 535 million animals are slaughtered in the Netherlands every year, more than 518 million of them chickens. Inspection figures cited in the report show that around 3 million birds arrive at slaughterhouses injured each year.

Two-thirds of 170 pig farms checked in 2023 and 2024 by the food and product safety watchdog NVWA were breaking welfare rules. The watchdog spends just 8% of its capacity on animal welfare.

The committee said the agriculture minister gives the sector too little direction and repeatedly delays decisions.

item.title: “Very dangerous”: Rights group condemns Kristallnacht speech
item.description:
“Very dangerous”: Rights group condemns Kristallnacht speech

November 10, 2026 Louis Gore-Langton

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Kristallnacht remembrance service in Amsterdam’s Portuguese Synagogue has stirred controversy after the keynote speaker condemned the Red Line protests and said labelling the Gaza war a genocide was rooted in anti-Semitism.

In a highly political speech, Chanan Hertzberger, chair of Jewish umbrella organisation CJO, denounced the “genocide lie” in front of a congregation containing senior cabinet members including the prime minister Rob Jetten, who also spoke.

Gerard Jonkman, director of Amsterdam-based Rights Forum, which campaigns on behalf of Palestinian rights, told Dutch News Hertzberger’s speech was “absolutely unacceptable”.

“This is also mixing the issue of anti-Semitism with criticism of Israel,” he said, “which is very, very, very dangerous.”

Hertzberger began his speech by thanking Jetten for not giving in to “the demands of the organisers of yesterday’s anti-Israel demonstration”, which he said amounted “directly or indirectly” to wiping Israel off the map.

“Who is being held responsible, in Arnhem, in Groningen and in Amsterdam for this so-called genocide?” he said. “We, the Jews. In our own own cities. In our streets. In our children’s classrooms. We are being ostracised and pushed to the margins of society.”

Only hours before, Jetten had spoken to RTL Nieuws saying it had been “impossible to miss” the protest and that he decided to stay away (having attended previous ones) because of his new role as PM, which he and his fellow cabinet member have used from the beginning to “increase pressure on Israel”.

“He embarrassed Jetten”

Jonkman said he thought Hertzberger had embarrassed Jetten and that the prime minister should now react to “these ridiculous accusations of hatred towards Israel.”

He said many Jewish people joined Sunday’s demonstration, among them Holocaust survivors and children of Holocaust survivors, and that many people he had spoken to were hurt by the speech.

Linking the protest to anti-Semitism in this way makes Jewish people in the Netherlands appear accountable for the policies of the Israeli government, he said.

Hertzberger said the “lie” that Israel was committing genocide now “marches weekly through our streets”, citing chants at Sunday’s protest, though he added that not all demonstrators were anti-Semites.

Zionism

He claimed that in fact the majority of Jewish people in the Netherlands are Zionists, that Zionism is the recognition of Israel’s right to exist as a “safe, independent Jewish state”, and that those things are now “more important than ever”.

He mentioned the numerous attacks on Jewish schools and synagogues in the Netherlands this year, and said that the images of Gaza left no one unmoved, including himself.

Hans Weijel, vice chairman of the CJO, told Dutch News that it is true a majority of Dutch-Jewish community are Zionists in the sense that they view Israel as a safe haven, but that does not mean they support what the Israeli government is doing in Gaza.

“That does not excuse that the safe haven should suppress other people. But we would like to have a place where we can go to and do not have to be on our knees and beg to be admitted to that country,” he said.

As to the Jewish people who don’t believe there needs to be a safe haven, he said he thinks they represent a small minority in the Netherlands and that this belief is potentially naive.

A United Nations commission of inquiry concluded in September 2025 that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, a finding Israel rejects.

The International Criminal Court in The Hague has issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and his former defence minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity. Both men have firmly denied the allegations.

Jetten’s premiership has marked a downturn in Dutch-Israeli relations. Since the cabinet enacted a ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territories in September, Israel has responded by stripping Dutch diplomats of their status and removing Dutch officials from a US-backed Gaza ceasefire centre.
